text:
Thomas Chabot is quietly running one of the better pairs in the league. Ottawa has 58% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 7.9 points better than when he sits, and he's playing almost 24 minutes a night.

The point total, eight in 14 games, undersells that. He has a four-game assist streak and only one goal on 1.6 expected, shooting 3.8% against a normal range around 6%. Defensemen's goals come in bunches; his haven't started yet.

He missed time in October (no games between Oct 17 and Oct 29) and came back on a lighter load, under 20 minutes in two games, before climbing back to 22 to 24. Evolving-Hockey had him 29th among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 16% of entries at his blue line (typical is 11%) and taking 27% of his shots off the rush, high for a defenseman. Our projection: about 43 points.
